claims.quote: A case may run its agent several times in the same folder, as work that a later session picks up. Its prompts are then a `sessions/` folder of files named by number, `1.md`, `2.md`, run in that order, and each later prompt gets the message the session before it ended with wherever it says `{{earlier}}`.

A case's `setup.mjs` makes the world around the sessions. It may export `start()`, called once before the runs, which returns what to `stop()` after them, such as a service the agents call; `prepare(work)`, which lays out a run's folder before its first session; `between(work, finished)`, called after each session but the last, for the changes the next session is not told about; and `finish(work, logs)`, which may leave a record beside the run's transcripts.
`--bare` runs the case with no skill at all.

A frozen eval of what a record of observations is worth when re-observing is expensive and nothing else says what changed. It runs in two sessions, and between them the project changes without the agent being told.

It pays most where what you observed is expensive to observe again, such as an eval, a benchmark, or a slow run, and nothing else says which files changed since: uncommitted work in the files, a shared working tree, a stash, a folder outside git.
`--from <folder>` runs a changed copy of the skill instead of the one in `skills/`, or another skill to compare it with; the agent is told the name its `SKILL.md` gives.
